xmldoc.short_description: Connect two block ports or physical pins in an nflow model.

param_input_item.param_description: a string: the name of the loaded nflow model.
a string 'Block/port': the source endpoint. A numbered port (for example 'Src/1') is a 1-based signal output port.
a string 'Block/port': the target endpoint, a 1-based signal input port.
a string 'Block/pin' with a named pin (for example 'R1/p', 'M1/flange'): a physical pin of an acausal block. Both endpoints must be named pins.

param_output_item.param_description: a handle to the created line.

description.p: add_line connects two block ports in an nflow model.

The kind of connection is chosen from the endpoints. A numbered endpoint such as 'Src/1' is a 1-based signal port; a named endpoint such as 'R1/p' or 'M1/flange' is a physical pin of an acausal block (electrical, thermal or mechanical). Both endpoints must be of the same kind; mixing a numbered port with a named pin raises an error.

Joining two physical pins makes them share one node (the acausal across/through variables are balanced there), so a physical connection has no fixed direction. To join three or more pins at a single node, make successive add_line calls that share a pin: they merge into the same node. Physical models require the 'dae' solver.

example_item.example_item_description: Physical pins (named endpoints). The last two calls share pin 'L1/n', so L1.n, C1.p and VS.p merge into one electrical node.
